## Timeline and Key Facts

The Austin City Council voted 8-2 on November 2, 2023, to eliminate minimum parking requirements, making Austin the largest city in the country to stop requiring new developments to have a set amount of parking.

The elimination included single-family homes, apartment buildings, offices and shopping malls. The ordinance took effect on November 12, 2023—10 days after it was passed by Council.

## What This Replaced

Previously, Austin had required every single-family home to have room to park at least two cars, and for apartments, the requirement was one-and-a-half spaces for a one-bedroom apartment plus half a space for every additional bedroom.

## Rationale

Affordable housing advocates, developers and climate activists say rules requiring a minimum amount of parking spaces on new projects drives up construction costs and enables a dependency on vehicles to get around town.

## Important Limitations

Getting rid of the requirements doesn't mean the city is abolishing parking altogether—developers still can decide how much parking they need, and the city will still require properties to comply with federal law and build accessible parking spaces for people living with disabilities.

# HOME Amendments: Phase 1 & Phase 2 Overview

## Phase 1 (Multiple Dwelling Units)

**Zoning Districts:** SF-1, SF-2, SF-3

**Allowed Unit Types:**
- Up to three housing units total per lot
- Includes tiny homes (≤400 sq ft, excluding loft space)
- Duplexes, two-unit, and three-unit residential uses
- Removes "primary vs. secondary" distinction for dwelling units

**Dimensional Standards:**

| Standard | Phase 1 Requirement |
|----------|-------------------|
| Max Building Coverage | 40% |
| Max Impervious Cover | 45% |
| Height Limit | Base zoning only (SF district limits no longer apply; Subchapter F's 32-ft restriction only applies to single-family use) |
| Unit Separation | None required by zoning; must comply with International Residential Code |
| FAR | Governed by existing GFA rules; enclosed space counts (garages, lofts, mezzanines included) |

**Key Regulation Changes:**
- Removes unrelated adult occupancy limits
- Every dwelling in two/three-unit uses requires unique address
- Preservation Bonus exempts preserved structures from GFA/FAR calculations

**Procedural Pathway:** Standard or Expedited residential building permit applications

**Timeline:**
- Adopted: December 7, 2023
- Applications accepted: February 5, 2024

---

## Phase 2 (Small Lot Single-Family Residential)

**Zoning Districts:** SF-1, SF-2, SF-3

**Allowed Unit Types:**
- One dwelling unit only on smaller lots (1,800–5,749 sq ft)
- Not eligible for Preservation Bonus

**Lot Size Requirements:**
"minimum lot area" of at least 1,800 square feet but less than 5,750 square feet

1. **Subdivision Applications** (required unless lot already <5,750 sq ft)
   - Residential Infill: streamlined process for re-subdivisions ≤1 acre meeting specific criteria
2. **Building Permits** (for existing compliant lots)

**Drainage Requirements (Residential Infill Projects):**
- Lots created before June 16, 2025: no drainage review needed for ≤4 units
- Lots created after June 16, 2025: compliance with grading plan required per modified standards

**Procedural Pathway:** Building permit or subdivision/infill plat applications

**Timeline:**
- Phase 2 adopted: May 16, 2024
- Applications accepted (limited): August 16, 2024
- Citywide (including WUI areas): November 16, 2024
- Site Plan Lite & Infill Plat adopted: March 6, 2025
- Applications accepted: June 16, 2025

## Key Points:

**Plat Building Lines vs. Zoning Setbacks:**

A recorded plat is a detailed map of a subdivision that has been reviewed and approved by the city or county and then recorded in the public records, and they are tied to the land itself and apply to every lot shown on that plat. Zoning setbacks are defined by your property's zoning district, and each zoning district has its own front, side, and rear yard requirements.

**Which Controls:**

The most restrictive setback applies. This means if a plat shows a 25-foot building line and zoning requires a different setback, whichever is more restrictive (farther from the property line) must be followed.

**Austin-Specific Requirements:**

Multiple Austin zoning districts, including SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, and SF-4B, have minimum front yard setbacks of 25 feet.

**Enforcement:**

Plat setbacks are shown on the recorded subdivision plat and are typically enforced by the city/county through the permitting and inspection process, while zoning setbacks are enforced by the city's planning/building department.

In summary, when there's a conflict between plat requirements and zoning setbacks, the more restrictive requirement controls.

| Standard | HOME Phase 1 (Duplex/Two-Unit) |
|---|---|
| Front yard setback | **15 ft** (reduced from 25 ft) |
| Street side yard setback | **10 ft** (reduced from 15 ft) |
| Interior side yard setback | **5 ft** (unchanged) |
| Rear yard setback | **5 ft** (reduced from 10 ft), excl. easements |
| Maximum height | **35 ft** |
| Maximum building coverage | **40%** |
| Maximum impervious cover | **45%** (or watershed limit, whichever is more restrictive) |
| FAR | **0.40:1** |
| Building separation (zoning) | **None required by zoning**; must comply with IRC fire-separation requirements |

**Citation:** [HOME Amendments -- Austin Development Services](https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/home-amendments); [AIA Austin HOME Phase 1 Summary](https://aiaaustin.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/HOME_Summary-FAQ_20240126-1039.pdf); [Maxable -- HOME Initiative](https://maxablespace.com/austins-home-initiative-shakes-up-adu-regulations-in-2024/)

| Max impervious cover (45%) | ~3,528 sq ft |

## 25-Foot Platted Building Line

The recorded plat for Scofield Subdivision shows a **25-foot building line** on the front of Lot 12.

**Interaction with HOME Phase 1 setbacks:**

- HOME Phase 1 reduces the zoning front setback to 15 ft for two-unit/duplex uses.
- However, a platted building line is a deed restriction recorded against the land. Under Austin practice, **the more restrictive requirement controls** -- meaning the 25 ft platted building line governs over the 15 ft zoning setback.
- To use the 15 ft front setback, the owner would need to **replat or amend the plat** to remove or reduce the building line, which requires subdivision review.

**Recommendation:** Confirm whether Austin treats the platted building line as enforceable through the permitting process or only as a private covenant. If enforceable, factor a 25 ft front setback into the building envelope. If a variance or replat is viable, the 15 ft setback could unlock additional depth.

Scofield Farms (78727) is a 1990s-era suburban subdivision in north Austin. Based on research, **no Neighborhood Conservation Combining District (NCCD) overlay applies** to this area. NCCDs in Austin are concentrated in older central neighborhoods (Hyde Park, Heritage, etc.) that were substantially built out over 30 years before adoption.

No Neighborhood Plan (NP) combining district appears to apply to this part of 78727.

The property is in the **Walnut Creek watershed**, classified as a **suburban watershed** in the Austin Watershed Protection Ordinance. For suburban watersheds:

- Single-family residential impervious cover: governed by zoning (45% for SF-2)
- The watershed ordinance impervious cover limit for suburban watersheds is generally 40-55% depending on use category
- The **more restrictive** of zoning or watershed limits applies
- For this property, the 45% zoning limit is likely the controlling standard

Scofield Farms may fall within or near the WUI boundary. As of November 16, 2024, HOME Phase 2 applications are accepted citywide including WUI areas. HOME Phase 1 (duplex) was not initially restricted by WUI. Confirm WUI status via Austin GIS.

## Parking

Austin City Council voted 8-2 on **November 2, 2023** (effective November 12, 2023) to **eliminate all minimum parking requirements** citywide. This applies to all use types including single-family, duplex, multifamily, commercial, and office.

**What this means for this duplex project:**

- **No minimum parking spaces are required by code.**
- ADA-accessible parking must still comply with federal law if applicable.
- As a practical matter, most duplex developers in suburban locations still provide **2 spaces per unit** (4 total) via driveways and/or garages, since market expectations in north Austin neighborhoods include vehicle parking.

## Procedural Pathway

### Site Plan Exemption

Under Austin LDC, **residential uses of four or fewer units are exempt from site plan requirements**. A duplex (2 units) qualifies for this exemption. No administrative site plan is required.

### Building Permit

The duplex can proceed via a **residential building permit** application through Austin Development Services (DSD). Under HOME Phase 1, applications have been accepted since February 5, 2024.

**Permit review path:**

1. **Residential Plan Review** -- submit building plans through Austin DSD
2. Plans reviewed for compliance with LDC dimensional standards, IRC/IBC building codes, and applicable environmental/drainage requirements
3. No zoning change, conditional use permit, or Board of Adjustment variance is needed (assuming the lot meets dimensional standards)

### Site Plan Lite (HOME Phase 2 -- March 2025)

Site Plan Lite is a streamlined review process adopted March 6, 2025, primarily for HOME Phase 2 subdivision and small-lot projects. It is **not required** for a duplex on an existing lot that already meets SF-2 minimum lot size. However, if the owner later pursues subdivision of the lot (e.g., into two small lots), Site Plan Lite would apply.

### Demolition Permit

A separate **demolition permit** is required to remove the existing house. Austin DSD processes demo permits administratively; typical turnaround is 2-4 weeks. Asbestos survey may be required for pre-2000 construction (this house was built 1993).

### Tree Permits

Austin's tree ordinance (LDC Ch. 25-8, Subchapter B) protects trees with trunk diameter >= 19 inches (heritage trees >= 24 inches). A tree survey may be required, and mitigation fees or replacement may apply if protected trees must be removed.

**Citation:** [Austin DSD -- Residential Plan Review](https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/residential-plan-review); [Austin DSD -- Site Plans and Exemptions](https://www.austintexas.gov/siteplans); [HOME Amendments Page](https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/home-amendments)

If enforced, the front setback is 25 ft (not 15 ft), reducing the buildable envelope by ~10 ft of depth.

3. **Lot width.** Confirm the lot width meets the 50 ft minimum required for duplex use. At 0.18 acres (~7,840 sq ft), the lot geometry needs verification from the plat.

4. **Watershed impervious cover.** Confirm the Walnut Creek suburban watershed impervious cover limit for this specific parcel. The 45% zoning limit is likely controlling, but verify via Austin's watershed GIS layer.

5. **HOA restrictions.** Scofield Farms has an HOA ($125/quarter per listing data). HOA covenants, conditions, and restrictions (CC&Rs) may prohibit or restrict duplex construction, impose architectural review, or set additional setback/height/design requirements independent of city zoning. Review the recorded CC&Rs and any deed restrictions on Lot 12, Block M.

6. **Tree survey.** Confirm whether any protected or heritage trees exist on the lot that would require mitigation.

7. **Drainage review.** For demolition and new construction on an existing lot (not a new subdivision), confirm whether drainage/grading plan review is required or if the project falls under the four-unit residential exemption.

## Summary Assessment

A ground-up duplex at 12713 Cinchring Ln is **permitted by right** under HOME Phase 1 on this SF-2 lot. The project can proceed via **residential building permit only** -- no rezoning, conditional use permit, site plan, or Board of Adjustment action is required. Key constraints are the 40% building coverage / 0.40 FAR cap, the 45% impervious cover limit, and the potential 25 ft front building line from the plat (versus the 15 ft HOME setback). The most significant non-zoning risk is the Scofield Farms HOA CC&Rs, which should be reviewed before design proceeds.
